chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad the just goldsmith narrated to us. He said: Isa ibn Muhammad al-Alawi narrated to us. He said: Abu Uwana narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Bazi al-Khazzaz narrated to us. He said: Ismail ibn Aban narrated to us, from Sallam ibn Abi Amra al-Khurasani, from Maruf ibn Kharbudh al-Makki, from Abu al-Tufayl Amir ibn Wathila, from Hudhayfa ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

O Hudhayfa! Indeed, the Proof of Allah upon you after me is Ali ibn Abi Talib. Disbelief in him is disbelief in Allah, associating partners with him is associating partners with Allah, doubt in him is doubt in Allah, heresy regarding him is heresy regarding Allah, denial of him is denial of Allah, and faith in him is faith in Allah -- for he is the brother of the Messenger of Allah, his deputy, the Imam of his nation and their master. He is the firm Rope of Allah and His firm Handle that has no crack in it. Two will be destroyed regarding him, to no fault of his: an excessive lover and one who falls short.

O Hudhayfa! Do not ever split away from Ali, for you will have split from me; and do not ever oppose Ali, for you will have opposed me. Indeed, Ali is from me and I am from him. Whoever angers him has angered me, and whoever pleases him has pleased me.

key_terms.العروة الوثقى: The Firm Handle -- a Quranic term (2:256, 31:22) for the unbreakable bond with God
key_terms.حبل الله المتين: The firm Rope of Allah -- a Quranic metaphor (3:103) for divine guidance
key_terms.حجة الله: The Proof of Allah -- a title denoting the divinely appointed authority on earth
key_terms.غال: Excessive (ghali) -- one who exaggerates the status of a figure beyond due bounds
key_terms.مقصر: One who falls short (muqassir) -- one who diminishes the rightful status of a figure
key_terms.وصي: Deputy/executor -- the designated successor of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the status of Ali ibn Abi Talib after him?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) addresses his companion Hudhayfa ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, declaring that Ali ibn Abi Talib is the Proof (hujja) of Allah after him, and that attitudes toward Ali are equivalent to attitudes toward God Himself. The Prophet employs Quranic imagery -- describing Ali as the 'firm rope of Allah' (habl Allah al-matin) and the 'firm handle' (al-urwa al-wuthqa) -- to underscore Ali's divinely appointed authority. This teaching was delivered in the context of establishing the post-prophetic leadership (Imamate) and warns against both extremism (ghuluww) and neglect (taqsir) in relation to Ali.
